entries.title: Hebrews 11:1
segments: Faith is the realization of things hoped for--the proof of things not seen.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:2
segments: And it was for faith that the men of old were renowned.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:3
segments: Faith enables us to perceive that the universe was created at the bidding of God--so that we know that what we see was not made out of visible things.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:4
segments: Faith made the sacrifice which Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain's, and won him renown as a righteous man, God himself establishing his renown by accepting his gifts; and it is by the example of his faith that Abel, though dead, still speaks.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:5
segments: Faith led to Enoch's removal from earth, that he might not experience death. 'He could not be found because God had removed him.' For, before his removal, he was renowned as having pleased God;

entries.title: Hebrews 11:6
segments: But without faith it is impossible to please him, for he who comes to God must believe that God exists, and that he rewards those who seek for him.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:7
segments: It was faith that enabled Noah, after he had received the divine warning about what could not then be foreseen, to build, in reverent obedience, an ark in which to save his family. By his faith he condemned the world, and became possessed of that righteousness which follows upon faith.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:8
segments: It was faith that enabled Abraham to obey the Call that he received, and to set out for the place which he was afterwards to obtain as his own; and he set out not knowing where he was going.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:9
segments: It was faith that made him go to live as an emigrant in the Promised Land--as in a strange country--living there in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who shared the promise with him.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:10
segments: For he was looking for the City with the sure foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:11
segments: Again, it was faith that enabled Sarah to conceive (though she was past the age for child-bearing), because she felt sure that he who had given her the promise would not fail her.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:12
segments: And so from one man--and that when his powers were dead--there sprang a people as numerous 'as the stars in the heavens or the countless grains of sand upon the shore.'

entries.title: Hebrews 11:13
segments: All these died sustained by faith. They did not obtain the promised blessings, but they saw them from a distance and welcomed the sight, and they acknowledged themselves to be only aliens and strangers on the earth.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:14
segments: Those who speak thus show plainly that they are seeking their fatherland.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:15
segments: If they had been thinking of the land that they had left, they could have found opportunities to return.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:16
segments: But no, they were longing for a better, a heavenly, land! And therefore God was not ashamed to be called their God; indeed he had already prepared them a city.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:17
segments: It was faith that enabled Abraham, when put to the test, to offer Isaac as a sacrifice--he who had received the promises offering up his only son,

entries.title: Hebrews 11:18
segments: of whom it had been said-- 'It is through Isaac that there shall be descendants to bear thy name.'

entries.title: Hebrews 11:19
segments: For he argued that God was able even to raise a man from the dead--and indeed, figuratively speaking, Abraham did receive Isaac back from the dead.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:20
segments: It was faith that enabled Isaac to bless Jacob and Esau, even with regard to the future.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:21
segments: Faith enabled Jacob, when dying, to give his blessing to each of the sons of Joseph, and 'to bow himself in worship as he leant upon the top of his staff.'

entries.title: Hebrews 11:22
segments: Faith caused Joseph, when his end was near, to speak of the future migration of the Israelites, and to give instructions with regard to his bones.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:23
segments: Faith caused the parents of Moses to hide the child for three months after his birth, for they saw that he was a beautiful child; and they would not respect the King's order.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:24
segments: It was faith that caused Moses, when he was grown up, to refuse the title of 'Son of a Daughter of Pharaoh.'

entries.title: Hebrews 11:25
segments: He preferred sharing the hardships of God's People to enjoying the short-lived pleasures of sin.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:26
segments: For he counted 'the reproaches that are heaped upon the Christ' of greater value than the treasures of Egypt, looking forward, as he did, to the reward awaiting him.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:27
segments: Faith caused him to leave Egypt, though undaunted by the King's anger, for he was strengthened in his endurance by the vision of the invisible God.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:28
segments: Faith led him to institute the Passover and the Sprinkling of the Blood, so that the Destroyer might not touch the eldest children of the Israelites.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:29
segments: Faith enabled the people to cross the Red Sea, as if it had been dry land, while the Egyptians, when they attempted to do so, were drowned.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:30
segments: Faith caused the walls of Jericho to fall after being encircled for seven days.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:31
segments: Faith saved Rahab, the prostitute, from perishing with the unbelievers, after she had entertained the spies with friendliness.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:32
segments: Need I add anything more? Time would fail me if I attempted to relate the stories of Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah, and those of David, Samuel, and the Prophets.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:33
segments: By their faith they subdued kingdoms, ruled righteously, gained the fulfilment of God's promises, 'shut the mouths of lions,'

entries.title: Hebrews 11:34
segments: quelled the fury of the flames, escaped the edge of the sword, found strength in the hour of weakness, displayed their prowess in war, and routed hostile armies.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:35
segments: Women received back their dead raised to life. Some were tortured on the wheel, and refused release in order that they might rise to a better life.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:36
segments: Others had to face taunts and blows, and even chains and imprisonment.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:37
segments: They were stoned to death, they were tortured, they were swan asunder, they were put to the sword; they wandered about clothed in the skins of sheep or goats, destitute, persecuted, ill-used--

entries.title: Hebrews 11:38
segments: men of whom the world was not worthy--roaming in lonely places, and on the mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.

entries.title: Hebrews 11:39
segments: Yet, though they all won renown by their faith, they did not obtain the final fulfilment of God's promise;

entries.title: Hebrews 11:40
segments: since God had in view some better thing for us, that they, apart from us, should not attain perfection.
